items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: The interviewee mentions a girl 'from New York' but does not mention a person named 'York'.

ctx.x: Did you always work with the club? Did you always work for a flat guarantee? Did you ever get a percentage of the tape? No, no percentage. The only time, you know, after I had hit records, records that would sell, and you would go out and play for, well, the booking agency would write a contract you would get.

Say, $5.50. $5.50. $5.50 was a good price for a recording office at that time. $5.50 and 50% over $1,100. See, so how they do, I make $5.50, the promoter would make $5.50, then we split the difference. Yeah. And I can remember Shell Booking Agency booking me in Shreveport, and that's the way the contract run. I think I made a few dollars over, yeah. Yeah. But you know what? This was white, not black, because this was on When I Meet My Girl. And you know, I was more popular up that way. You know what I was doing?…
Did you always have to be, did you watch yourself, like if you were approached by a white girl?
